references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, instructions are given that ordinary priests must not make themselves unclean by contact with a dead body, except for close relatives. Verse 11 tightens this rule for the high priest, who may not even become unclean for his father or mother.
The Nazirite had similar restrictions and was not to come near any dead body, not even for father, mother, brother, or sister, because his consecration to God was upon his head.

Detailed laws about uncleanness from touching a corpse. Anyone who touches a dead body becomes unclean for seven days, which explains the background for the prohibition against the high priest approaching the dead.
Ezekiel's vision of the future temple contains similar rules for priests regarding uncleanness from contact with corpses, with exceptions only for immediate family members.
After the death of Nadab and Abihu, Aaron and his surviving sons were commanded not to mourn or leave the tabernacle, because the Lord's anointing oil was upon them.
